sentences.text: This is the first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of bail.

The applicant is in custody since 17.12.2021 in connection with Crime No.22/2016 registered at Police Station E.O.W., District Bhopal (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under sections 420, 409, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code of 1860.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 17.12.2021.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
The main culprits are the Directors and Owners of the Company.
Applicant has already resigned from the Company in the year 2012, which was accepted in the year 2013 while the offence is said to be commenced on 2016.

Copy of the resignation and its acceptance Anil Kumar Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14911567/
1 is annexed hereto.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applicant has already been enlarged on bail from the different Courts including the High Court of Chattisgarh, Sessions Court and High Court of Madhya Pradesh also.
The prosecution story is frivolous and FIR has been made against the applicant only in order
to harass

. 
There is no material to establish the intention of the applicant for such act.
Co-ordinate Bench of this Court has been enlarged the applicant on bail in the similar offence vide order dated 27.01.2023 passed in MCRC No.3483/2023.
Present applicant is also the victim of the fraud done by the Company Owners.
Hence, he prays that applicant be enlarged on bail.
Per contra, learned Special Public Prosecutor for the EOW opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that applicant is the prime accused in the aforesaid offence.
So many offences have been registered against the present applicant for committing such type of fraud with the investors throughout the India.
Therefore, he does not deserve for bail.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that offence has been committed with 3199 investors and money involved in the instant case is more than Rs.15 Crores, applicant is named in the FIR, the facts that he has resigned from the post of Director and its acceptance is matter of evidence, so many criminal offences have been registered against the applicant and other co-accused persons throughout the India for the similar nature crime.
In view of the above, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the present applicant.
Accordingly, this present bail application preferred under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is hereby rejected.
Certified copy as per rules.
